idea: This is SplitBeacon, my displays week project.
The idea is a lap timer that makes pacing visible without unlocking a phone.
Two RGB panels show interval progress and recent split history, while a small screen shows exact times.
Buttons record laps, pause the timer, and change views. Knobs set the target and brightness.
These images are concept and CAD previews from the project files, not a physical prototype.
The next step is assembly and real hardware testing. This narration uses my existing local synthetic voice model.
progress: This is the SplitBeacon design walkthrough, using the actual project files.
The custom controller connects a Pico, two RGB panels, a TFT, buttons and analog controls.
The timer keeps paused time out of a split and latches the target at the start of each lap.
The package contains firmware checks, a routed board, fabrication exports, and printable enclosure parts.
The recorded checks do not establish physical performance. Current draw, display orientation, and printed fit still need bench testing.
This is a design walkthrough, not evidence of five hours worked. The narration is synthetic.
